items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal retirement was not just about Jorge Jesus as journalist reveals whether CR7 could return under new coach
items.description:
Although his public fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus dominated the headlines, comments from a journalist close to the Al-Nassr star suggest there may be more to the story than a disagreement over playing time. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s decision to end his Portugal career has raised questions about whether the legendary forward could ever reconsider his international retirement. Although his public fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus dominated the headlines, comments from a journalist close to the Al-Nassr star suggest there may be more to the story than a disagreement over playing time.



With Ronaldo having spent 23 years representing his country, many supporters would welcome the opportunity to see him receive a more fitting farewell. However, the possibility of a return could depend on more than a change in the coaching staff.



Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5, 2026, bringing an end to a Portugal career that produced 234 appearances and a record 146 goals. The announcement came after tensions with Jesus, who had previously coached the forward at Al-Nassr before taking charge of the national team.



The disagreement reportedly intensified during the September international break. Ronaldo started his nation’s 1-0 victory over Wales but was left on the bench throughout the subsequent match against Norway, despite warming up for an extended period.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal walks to the bench as a substitute



The situation eventually led to Ronaldo leaving the national team camp. The Portuguese Football Federation subsequently handed him a 30-day suspension and a €255 fine, while the forward later confirmed that he would no longer represent Portugal.



Jorge Jesus expected Ronaldo to return



Jesus maintained that he had intended to include Ronaldo in his plans for the November international fixtures and said he was unaware of the retirement decision before the public announcement. The Portugal coach also insisted that he felt no guilt over his decisions, arguing that he had acted in the team’s best interests.



The coaching staff and federation president Pedro Proenca reportedly attempted to persuade Ronaldo to reconsider. Their efforts were unsuccessful, leaving Portugal without its most prolific international goalscorer ahead of the next Nations League matches.



Would Ronaldo return if Portugal appointed a different coach?



Portuguese journalist Pedro Sepulveda, who is close to Ronaldo, has now addressed whether the situation could change if Jesus eventually left his position. Asked whether the forward might have continued representing Portugal under a different coach, Sepulveda suggested that Ronaldo would have retired from international soccer regardless of who was in charge. “No, no, I think that in terms of playing for the national team, Ronaldo wouldn’t play again even if the coach were different,” Sepulveda explained.



Roberto Martinez, Head Coach of Portugal, speaks to players at the hydration break.



The journalist nevertheless indicated that the circumstances surrounding Ronaldo’s departure involved several factors and people. He suggested that the forward had wanted an opportunity to say goodbye to Portugal on his own terms, but the events surrounding his final appearances left him disappointed.



Sepulveda also suggested that Ronaldo felt many people wanted to see him continue playing for the national team. However, the situation had become complicated enough that simply replacing Jesus would not necessarily persuade the 41-year-old to reverse his decision.



Although Sepulveda does not expect Ronaldo to return as an active international player, his comments leave room for the possibility of a different kind of ending. He indicated that supporters may have to wait until Jesus leaves the national team before circumstances change sufficiently for a more fitting farewell to be considered.

items.title: Manchester City’s weaknesses under Enzo Maresca are being exposed
items.description: After three straight defeats, City’s manager says he will use the international break to reassess. Their problems may go beyond tacticsSign up for our free newsletter hereEnzo Maresca seemed, if not quite baffled by his side’s Saturday defeat to Nottingham Forest, then at least a little put out. After seven straight wins from the start of the season, that’s now three straight defeats, a pattern so unusual that it’s been recorded only once before in top-flight English history, by Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05. The three defeats were all different, Maresca said, although in all of them City had had more possession and more chances.In the 2-1 defeat at Aston Villa two weeks ago, City had 63% of the ball and had 15 chances to Villa’s eight. In the 1-0 home defeat to Brighton last weekend, they had 62% possession and 21 chances to seven. At the City Ground, it was 79% possession and 12 chances to 11. So Maresca is right in one way: City could look at basic statistics and say they had been unfortunate – although Forest could equally point to the fact that they went into that game third top of the expected goals table but second-bottom of the actual table.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. items.title: That’s a Mora: Rodrigo and Roma rise with Lazio to give Eternal City new life | Nicky Bandini
items.description: Roma and Lazio have both made unbeaten starts to the Serie A season, giving those in the Italian capital dreams of a ScudettoAfter nine games in 28 days, Gian Piero Gasperini finally got a moment to pause and reflect on Sunday night. The Roma manager was back in Liguria, where he worked for the best part of a decade across two stints at Genoa, to collect an award from Stelle Nello Sport – an association formed to promote sport in the region – celebrating his career achievements and commitment to courageous attacking football.The timing worked out well. Gasperini’s Roma thumped Sassuolo 3-0 on Saturday, bouncing back from a midweek defeat against Manchester United. That result meant the Giallorossi had scored 31 times in 11 Serie A games. In the past 65 years only two Italian teams – the Juventus and Napoli sides of 2017-18 – had made a more prolific start to a top-flight campaign. More importantly, Roma’s victory meant they remained undefeated in domestic competition this season. Just like their neighbours Lazio, who drew 1-1 away against Napoli in the early kick-off on Sunday. Continue reading...

items.title: Felix Nmecha’s faith is forcing Borussia Dortmund into an uncomfortable debate
items.description: Midfielder’s spectacular strikes rescued a frustrating day, only for celebrations to reignite dialogue that has followed him through his careerIt was just what they needed at just the right time. For a tricky first half and beyond, Elversberg had been a stone in Borussia Dortmund’s shoe, the promoted side not just keeping the home team at bay but keeping them honest, nourishing ambitions of their own. “The fatigue was clearly visible,” the sporting director, Ole Book, said to Sky after a week which had contained Der Klassiker in Munich and a hard-fought Champions League victory against Betis. “We were a bit too focused on managing the game, which was understandable.”Enter Felix Nmecha. BVB have enjoyed a largely excellent start to the season, are unbeaten and level on points with Bayern Munich at the top; Bayern lead, unsurprisingly, thanks to their superior goal difference. It is a gap which has been widened by Dortmund being far from prolific, a facet which looked as if it might undercut their efforts to roll over their visitors on Saturday, especially in the absence of the injured centre-forward Serhou Guirassy. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo is the odd one out as Lionel Messi and Neymar share curious detail from their final international games
items.description:
heir departures came in very different circumstances, but a curious connection between their final international appearances has added another layer to the end of an era. 
Cristiano Ronaldo joined Lionel Messi and Neymar in bringing his international career to an end in 2026, marking an extraordinary year for soccer after three of the sport’s biggest names stepped away from their national teams. Their departures came in very different circumstances, but a curious connection between their final international appearances has added another layer to the end of an era.



Neymar‘s farewell followed Brazil’s elimination from the 2026 World Cup, while Messi received an emotional send-off in front of Argentina supporters. Ronaldo’s departure from Portugal was more complicated, with tensions surrounding his relationship with coach Jorge Jesus and the Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) attracting attention.



Santos’ captain was the first of the trio to bring his international career to a close. The Brazilian had indicated that the 2026 World Cup would be his final tournament with the Selecao, and he made his last appearance in the round of 16 against Norway.



Despite Brazil suffering a 2-1 defeat, Neymar found the net, scoring a late goal that ended the national team’s remarkable 79-match scoring streak. The result meant his final international appearance came in a painful elimination, although he still managed to leave the tournament with one last goal for his country.



🚨 End of an era. Neymar has announced his retirement from international football with Brazil.“I tried. I tried. It started here at MetLife Stadium and I finished here. It is now over.”From his 2010 debut at the same stadium to tonight’s heartbreaking 2-1 R16 exit vs Norway… pic.twitter.com/kmUHNYuHiG— Dr RK Singh (@DrRupak) July 6, 2026



Messi‘s farewell unfolded in much happier circumstances. Following Argentina’s World Cup final defeat, the legendary captain decided to end his international career, with the national team arranging a memorable send-off against Benin at the Monumental. Argentina won 3-0, with the 39-year-old superstar scoring once and providing two assists in front of an emotional home crowd.









Ronaldo’s Portugal farewell takes different turn



Ronaldo’s international retirement came later in the year, officially ending his extraordinary career with Portugal on November 5, 2026. His departure followed a turbulent period involving his exit from the national team’s October camp and subsequent reconciliation with Jorge Jesus.



The announcement arrived shortly before Jorge Jesus’ November squad selection, adding to speculation about the relationship between the captain, the coach and the federation. Unlike Messi, Ronaldo has so far shown little interest in arranging a dedicated farewell match.



Cristiano Ronaldo #7 of Portugal applauds fans



His final international goal had come earlier in the 2026 World Cup, when he helped Portugal secure a 2-1 comeback victory over Croatia in the round of 32. However, his final appearance for the national team would ultimately prove different from those of his two fellow superstars.



The curious stat separating Ronaldo from Messi and Neymar



There is a striking distinction between the three legends when looking at the matches that marked the end of their international careers. Ronaldo was the only member of the trio who failed to score in his final appearance for his national team.



Cristiano Ronaldo #7 of Portugal shows dejection



Neymar scored against Norway despite Brazil’s elimination, while Messi found the net during Argentina‘s 3-0 victory over Benin. Ronaldo, meanwhile, finished his Portugal career without adding another goal to his international record after his final strike against Croatia.



Los tres se retiraron de sus selecciones el mismo año. Su último gol fue de penalti y los tres lo patearon hacia el mismo lado.Cosas del destino y sus caprichos. pic.twitter.com/9a2usO4GpW— ALXN ❄️ (@alansitoo_20) November 6, 2026 



Yet another remarkable coincidence connects the three players: each scored his final international goal from the penalty spot. The accompanying video highlights the similarities between their last successful penalties, with Neymar and Messi reportedly sending their efforts towards the same side while Ronaldo opted for the center.

items.title: Atletico Madrid vs Barcelona: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 LaLiga match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Atletico Madrid vs Barcelona in the 2026-27 LaLiga. Atletico Madrid host Barcelona in a LaLiga clash that carries real weight near the top of the table, with Diego Simeone’s side looking to keep pace and Hansi Flick’s group chasing another statement win.
Atletico Madrid come into this one on a run of three straight wins, beating Levante 2-0 on October 31, Deportivo 1-0 on October 24 and Espanyol 1-0 on October 17. None of those results have come with much margin, but the clean sheets in all three show a side built on a solid defensive base under Simeone. A fourth straight win would send a strong signal that Atletico Madrid belong in the title picture.
Barcelona arrive off a 6-1 rout of Alaves last Saturday, a result that followed a 1-2 loss to Real Madrid on October 25 and a 5-2 win over Betis back on October 17. The scoreline against Alaves points to an attack firing on all cylinders, even if the defeat to their fiercest rival is still fresh. A win at the Metropolitano would answer any lingering questions after that loss and keep Barcelona firmly in the title race.
Atletico Madrid confirmed lineup
Simeone sets Atletico Madrid up in a 4-2-3-1, with Jan Oblak behind a back line of Marcos Llorente, Dávid Hancko, Marc Pubill and Álex Grimaldo. Koke and Pablo Barrios sit as the double pivot, giving the team cover to let Lee Kang-in, Giuliano Simeone and Álex Baena work around Julián Alvarez up top. Johnny is out, but the rest of the group is otherwise at full strength and set up to stay compact before looking to spring forward through Alvarez and Baena.
Atletico Madrid confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Jan Oblak, Marcos Llorente, Alejandro Grimaldo, Koke, Marc Pubill, Dávid Hancko, Giuliano Simeone, Pablo Barrios, Julián Alvarez, Lee Kang-In, Álex Baena. Coach: Diego Simeone.
Barcelona confirmed lineup
Flick also goes with a 4-2-3-1 for Barcelona, built around Joan García in goal and a back four of Brian Fariñas Pérez, Pau Cubarsí, Gerard Martín and João Cancelo. Marc Bernal and Pedri anchor midfield, feeding Fermín López, Lamine Yamal and Anthony Gordon behind Raphinha. The absences of Dani Olmo, Xavi Espart, Roony Bardghji and Juan Hernández thin out Flick’s attacking options from the bench, putting extra weight on the front four to create and finish chances against a well organized Atletico Madrid defense.
Barcelona confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Joan García, Brian Fariñas, João Cancelo, Marc Bernal, Pau Cubarsí, Gerard Martín, Pedri, Fermín López, Raphinha, Lamine Yamal, Anthony Gordon. Coach: Hansi Flick.

items.title: Manchester United vs Aston Villa: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Manchester United vs Aston Villa in the 2026-27 Premier League. Manchester United host Aston Villa with both sides looking to settle unsettled form, and this one carries weight well beyond the typical early-November fixture.
Manchester United come into this one off three straight defeats in all competitions, having lost 0-2 to Chelsea on October 31 and 0-3 to Bournemouth on October 25, with a 1-1 draw against Leeds on October 18 sandwiched between. That run leaves them without a win in their last three and searching for answers under Michael Carrick. A home game against Villa now looks like a chance to stop the slide rather than extend it.
Aston Villa arrive in much better shape, unbeaten in their last three matches. Unai Emery’s side beat Newcastle 1-0 on October 17 and followed that by beating Manchester City 2-1 on October 24, then drew 1-1 with Fulham on October 31. A positive result at Old Trafford would stretch that run further and reinforce Villa’s case as one of the form teams in the division right now.
Manchester United confirmed lineup
Carrick sets Manchester United up in a 4-2-3-1, with Senne Lammens behind a back line of Diogo Dalot, Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven and Harry Maguire. Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans sit as the double pivot, shielding a back four that has shipped goals in each of the last two games. Ahead of them, Bruno Fernandes operates centrally behind Matheus Cunha, flanked by Amad Diallo and Bryan Mbeumo, giving the attack width and combination play through the final third. The team is missing a significant chunk of its squad depth, with Marcus Rashford, Benjamin Šeško, Manuel Ugarte, Lisandro Martínez, Luke Shaw and Patrick Dorgu all out, which limits Carrick’s options both in attack and across the back line.
Manchester United confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Senne Lammens, Leny Yoro, Harry Maguire, Noussair Mazraoui, Diogo Dalot, Kobbie Mainoo, Bruno Fernandes, Youri Tielemans, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo. Coach: Michael Carrick.
Aston Villa confirmed lineup
Emery mirrors the hosts with a 4-2-3-1, Zion Suzuki starting behind Ian Maatsen, Pau Torres, Victor Lindelöf and Lamare Bogarde. Boubacar Kamara and Johan Manzambi anchor midfield, with Leon Goretzka pushed into a more advanced role. Alysson Edward Alysson and John McGinn support Nicolas Jackson in attack, giving Villa pace and movement to work off the lone striker. Villa are without Matty Cash, Amadou Onana, Matteo Ruggeri and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, which thins out their full back and defensive midfield options, but the rest of the lineup carries the same personnel that has driven their unbeaten run.
Aston Villa confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Zion Suzuki, Taylor Harwood-Bellis, Victor Lindelöf, Pau Torres, Ian Maatsen, Boubacar Kamara, Johan Manzambi, Leon Goretzka, Alysson Edward Alysson, Nicolas Jackson, John McGinn. Coach: Unai Emery.

Take a look at the projected lineups for Genoa vs AC Milan in the 2026-27 Serie A. Genoa host AC Milan at a moment when both sides arrive full of confidence, and this one has the look of a genuine measuring-stick fixture for the home side.
Genoa have won three straight, beating Lecce 2-1 on November 1 after a 2-0 win over Juventus on October 28 and a 1-0 result against Venezia FC on October 25. That stretch includes a statement win over Juventus, and De Rossi’s side will want to show that was no fluke against another top club. A victory here would extend their run to four games and keep them firmly in the upper half of the table conversation.
AC Milan head into this match off a 3-1 win over Inter on October 31, bouncing back from a 2-4 loss to Bologna on October 28 after beating Udinese 2-0 on October 25. The Inter result shows Milan can still produce big performances even after a setback, and Amorim will be looking for more consistency from his team. Another win on the road would steady the ship and keep Milan’s season on track after that loss to Bologna.

items.title: Kylian Mbappe’s scoring run at Real Madrid puts him on the trail of a Cristiano Ronaldo record
items.description:
Kylian Mbappe’s form with Real Madrid is putting him in the same conversation as Cristiano Ronaldo, with streaks in LaLiga and the Champions League that few players in the club’s history have reached. 
Kylian Mbappe keeps finding the net at the right moments for Real Madrid. On Saturday, the French forward sealed a 3-0 win over Valencia at Mestalla, stretching his tally to 13 LaLiga goals this season and getting closer and closer to an impressive Cristiano Ronaldo record.



According to data shared by football statistics account MisterChip, Mbappe has now scored in seven consecutive games for Real Madrid in all official competitions, and the streak is still alive.



That puts him within reach of a mark that belongs to Cristiano Ronaldo: the Portuguese forward appears twice in the same list with runs of 12 consecutive games with a goal, one in 2014 and another in 2018, the longest among Madrid players with streaks of seven or more in recent years.



The rest of the list shows how few players have gotten close. Mbappe himself reached eight in a row in 2025, while Karim Benzema had two runs of seven, in 2021 and 2022. Ronaldo, on the other hand, dominates the older part of the ranking, with a streak of 10 in 2014, two of eight in 2012 and 2013, and another of seven in 2012.




Mbappé scores (this was a scheduled tweet) ⏰ pic.twitter.com/51OB6dmg9w— Real Madrid C.F. 🇬🇧🇺🇸 (@realmadriden) November 7, 2026




For Mbappe, matching Ronaldo’s 12 would mean scoring in five more consecutive games, and he would need six to pass him. It is a long way to go, but he is the one who has come closest to Ronaldo’s streaks since the Portuguese left the club, and the way he is playing makes it a story worth following in the coming weeks.



A flying start in LaLiga and Europe


        


Mbappe has made scoring look routine in LaLiga. After the win at Mestalla, he has 13 goals and two assists in 12 league matches, trailing only Barcelona’s Raphinha, who stands at the top with 15 goals.



His numbers in the Champions League are just as good. Mbappe has scored in all four of Real Madrid’s league-phase matches, adding one assist, and the run goes back further: his goal against AEK Athens was his sixth in a row in the competition, tying the best streak of his career, set with PSG in 2022.



That Champions League run has put him in the same conversation as Cristiano Ronaldo. Until this week, the Portuguese forward was the only Real Madrid player to have scored in six or more straight matches in the competition, and his mark of 11 will be hard to match. 



With Real Madrid among the title contenders in LaLiga and unbeaten so far in the Champions League, Mbappe has every chance to keep adding to his numbers. Each match gives him another opportunity to extend his runs in Spain and Europe, and to keep moving closer to the marks left by Cristiano Ronaldo.

items.title: Lionel Messi reaches a new personal record with Inter Miami in the regular season finale
items.description:
Lionel Messi’s number for the finale is only part of the story, as the Inter Miami captain also heads into the last day of the regular season with a chance to achieve a pair of firsts that no player has ever managed in the history of MLS. 
Lionel Messi is about to close the 2026 MLS regular season with a mark he had never reached since joining Inter Miami. According to insider José Armando, the captain is set to play his 31st regular-season match of the year against Charlotte FC, the most appearances he has had in a single MLS season with the club.



The previous high was 28 matches in 2025, when Messi scored 29 goals and provided 19 assists on his way to the MLS Golden Boot and the MVP award. This year he arrived at the finale with 30 league appearances, and the MLS Golden Boot tracker had him at 2,574 minutes played, a sign of how much Inter Miami have leaned on their captain throughout a long campaign.



His workload has also come with production. Messi entered the final day at the top of the scoring chart with 26 goals, four more than Dallas forward Petar Musa, and with 14 assists.



The match that will give Messi a personal record also has a lot at stake for Inter Miami in the standings. The team moved into second place after beating New England 2-1 on the road, and a win over Charlotte would guarantee that position, leaving them well placed heading into the playoffs.




VAMOS MIAMI 🩷🖤 pic.twitter.com/3tOTjv7IDt— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) November 7, 2026




Messi on the verge of two feats no MLS player has pulled off



Messi’s final day in the regular season could add two more entries to his list of firsts in MLS, starting with the Golden Boot. He enters Decision Day with 26 goals and one more scoring title would make him the first player in the league’s 31-year history to win it in two consecutive seasons.


        


The other milestone within reach is the MVP award. Messi is the main candidate to collect his third in only three full seasons with Inter Miami, which has never been done in MLS. He already has two, and a third would leave him alone at the top of the league’s most prestigious individual honor.



Whatever happens against Charlotte, the focus will soon move to the playoffs, which begin on Nov. 18. If both awards end up in his hands, Messi would finish the year with the kind of double that no one before him has achieved in the league.

items.title: FIFA cuts suspension for Argentina’s Nahuel Molina but keeps Leandro Paredes’ ban over World Cup final incidents
items.description:
Nahuel Molina now has one game left to serve, while Leandro Paredes will be unavailable for Argentina until at least September 2027, and the Argentine Football Association is heading to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to seek a new review of the decision. 
Months after the World Cup final, the incidents that followed Spain’s 1-0 win over Argentina are still making headlines. FIFA’s Appeals Committee ruled on Friday on the appeal filed by the Argentine Football Association (AFA), partially accepting it: Nahuel Molina’s suspension was reduced, but Leandro Paredes’ ban was left untouched.



In Molina’s case, the right back’s suspension went from seven matches to four, while his fine dropped from 90,000 to 60,000 dollars. The national team has already played three games with him suspended, during the October FIFA window against Bolivia, Benin and Burkina Faso, so he has one match left to serve with Argentina.



Paredes did not get the same treatment. FIFA upheld the 10-match suspension and the 90,000-dollar fine that the Disciplinary Committee had imposed on him in August, after his clash with Spanish players Eric Garcia and Gavi following the final.



Of those ten games, three have been served and the midfielder will be unavailable for Argentina at least until September 2027. In August, FIFA also agreed to the AFA’s request that suspended matches be counted in friendlies and official CONMEBOL games.



Leandro Paredes #5 of Argentina and Eric Garcia #4 of Spain have words after the World Cup 2026 Final. (Getty Images)



The AFA also faces penalties and heads to CAS



The ruling was not only about the players. The Appeals Committee also upheld the fines imposed on the AFA over discriminatory chants heard during the tournament, according to the association’s statement.



Those sanctions came from the Disciplinary Committee’s August decision, which included a 321,000-dollar fine and matches with restricted attendance for Argentina, applied after incidents in the team’s games against Cape Verde, Egypt, Switzerland, England and Spain.



The August decision also reached members of the Argentine delegation: Thiago Almada received a one-match suspension, while staff member Roberto Ayala was given a three-match ban.



The AFA said it will now request the grounds for the decisions and take the case to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), considering that it has sufficient arguments of fact and law to seek a new review. For now, Paredes’ 10-match suspension and the fines remain in force, while Molina is closer to returning, with one game left to serve.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s No. 7 Portugal shirt may be in limbo as Rafael Leao suffers injury scare
items.description:
Rafael Leao’s injury scare leaves Portugal’s No. 7 up in the air, and Pedro Neto, Joao Felix and Francisco Trincao are among the names who have worn the number. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s No. 7 shirt with the Portugal national team may have to wait for its next wearer. A few days after Ronaldo’s retirement from international football, Rafael Leao was forced off injured during Galatasaray’s win over Amedspor, which raises doubts about his availability for the next international window.



On Saturday, in the Turkish Super Lig, Leao opened the scoring in the seventh minute, but in the 50th he went down after a backheel pass, grabbed his right leg and was replaced by Deniz Gul. 



Portuguese outlets such as Record and O Jogo described the problem as a muscle issue in the right thigh, although there is no official diagnosis or recovery timeline yet. The timing is a concern for Portugal, as Jorge Jesus called Leao up for the Nations League games during the international break.



Leao appears to be a candidate to succeed Ronaldo, as the No. 7 has already passed through his hands once. On Oct. 1, ahead of the Nations League match in Denmark, Ronaldo left Portugal’s camp in Copenhagen and the Galatasaray forward wore the No. 7 against Denmark and gave his usual No. 17 to Fabio Silva.




Sempre connosco. Obrigado, Portugueses. ❤️‍🔥 pic.twitter.com/qruLL2zbZ4— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) October 1, 2026




Who else could wear the No. 7?



Leao is not the only Portuguese attacker who is familiar with the number, and other players are also candidates to take the shirt. Pedro Neto wears the No. 7 at Chelsea, a shirt he has kept for 2026-27 after taking it over in 2024-25. For Portugal he currently wears the No. 18, but his style fits what the number has historically asked for.


        


Joao Felix is another candidate who has already worn the No. 7, at Atletico Madrid, although he wears the No. 11 with the national team and is unlikely to change his number.



Francisco Trincao is another name connected to the number, as he wears it for Al Ahli. Reports from Portugal also mention two younger options: Geovany Quenda, the Chelsea signing who still has to make his debut for the senior team, and Rodrigo Mora, the 19-year-old Roma midfielder who has been called up but has not played for the senior side yet.



For now, there is no official decision on who will carry the shirt that Cristiano Ronaldo wore for 23 years. The symbolism will always remain tied to the legendary forward, but because UEFA requires squads in league-phase Nations League matches to be numbered from 1 to 23, Portugal will have to name someone to wear it.

A fourth consecutive win would stretch that run and keep the pressure on anyone chasing them at the top.
Hull come into this one without a win in their last three outings, drawing 2-2 with Ipswich Town on October 31 and 1-1 with Brentford on October 25 after a 0-1 loss to Fulham on October 17. The draws at least show some resistance, but Sergej Jakirović’s side have not found a way to close games out. Three points at the Emirates would be a major statement, but even a point would count as a solid return against this opponent.
Arsenal confirmed lineup
Arteta sets Arsenal up in a 4-2-3-1 with David Raya behind a back four of Jurriën Timber, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães and Riccardo Calafiori. Declan Rice and Bruno Guimarães sit in front of them, giving the team control in midfield, while Martín Odegaard operates just ahead in support of Kai Havertz up top. Noni Madueke and Christos Tzolis provide width and pace on the flanks. The absences of Bukayo Saka and William Saliba are notable, along with Louie Copley and Max Dowman also out, but the depth on show suggests Arsenal are well equipped to cope.
Arsenal confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): David Raya, Jurriën Timber, Riccardo Calafiori, Bruno Guimarães, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel Magalhães, Noni Madueke, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz, Martin Ødegaard, Christos Tzolis. Coach: Mikel Arteta.
Hull confirmed lineup
Jakirović goes with a defensive 5-4-1 shape, built around a back five of Lewie Coyle, Semi Ajayi, John Egan, Nobel Mendy and Ryan Giles protecting goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis. Mohamed Belloumi, Tim Iroegbunam, Regan Slater and Elliot Stroud make up a packed midfield four tasked with limiting the space Arsenal’s attackers can work in. Oli McBurnie leads the line alone, relying on quick counters to create any threat. Hull are missing a long list of players including Matthew Targett, Eliot Matazo, Charlie Hughes, Jack Butland, Lucas Gourna-Douath, Ilyas Ansah, Darko Gyabi and Sorba Thomas, which explains the cautious setup and the emphasis on numbers behind the ball.
Hull confirmed starting XI (5-3-2): Konstantinos Tzolakis, Lewie Coyle, Elliot Stroud, Nobel Mendy, John Egan, Semi Ajayi, Tim Iroegbunam, Lucas Gourna-Douath, Oliver McBurnie, Mohamed-Ali Cho, Regan Slater. Coach: Sergej Jakirović.

items.title: Leeds vs Tottenham: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Premier League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Leeds vs Tottenham in the 2026-27 Premier League. Leeds and Tottenham arrive at this one going in opposite directions, and that contrast should shape how the game is played out.
Leeds have gone three games without a win, losing 0-2 to Bournemouth on October 31 after draws with Sunderland and Man U. The 0-0 with Sunderland on October 25 followed a 1-1 share of the points with Man U on October 18, and neither result did much to settle any nerves at Elland Road. A home game against one of the league’s form sides is a tough way to try to snap out of it.
Tottenham could hardly be in better shape, winning three straight without conceding, including a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace on October 31. Before that they beat Chelsea 2-0 on October 24 and put three past Coventry on October 19 in a 3-1 win. A fourth consecutive victory would send a strong message that Tottenham belong among the league’s top sides this season.
Leeds confirmed lineup
Daniel Farke sets Leeds up in a 3-4-2-1, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin as the focal point up front and Brenden Aaronson and Harry Wilson tasked with supplying him from deeper positions. Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka anchor the midfield, giving the side some control before the ball is worked out to wing-backs Jayden Bogle and Gabriel Gudmundsson. Leeds are without Noah Okafor, Joe Rodon and Mateo Joseph, which thins out both the forward line and central defensive cover, with Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemović left to marshal the back three in Rodon’s absence.
Leeds confirmed starting XI (3-4-2-1): James Trafford, Nico Elvedi, Tarik Muharemović, James Justin, Jayden Bogle, Lukas Nmecha, Ethan Ampadu, Sean Longstaff, Gabriel Gudmundsson, Ao Tanaka, Dominic Calvert-Lewin. Coach: Daniel Farke.
Tottenham confirmed lineup
Roberto De Zerbi lines Tottenham up in a 4-2-3-1, with Mathys Tel leading the line and Mohammed Kudus, James Maddison and Omar Marmoush working in support behind him. Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes sit in front of the back four, screening a defense that includes Micky van de Ven and Jan-Paul van Hecke in the middle. The absentee list is long, with Tosin Adarabioyo, Lucas Bergvall, Wilson Odobert, Mykhaylo Mudryk, Savinho, Xavi Simons, Rodrigo Bentancur and Richarlison all out, but the players coming in have kept the team winning regardless.
Tottenham confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Antonín Kinský, Pedro Porro, Jan-Paul van Hecke, Micky van de Ven, Andy Robertson, Sandro Tonali, Archie Gray, Mateus Fernandes, Mohammed Kudus, Omar Marmoush, Mathys Tel. Coach: Roberto De Zerbi.

items.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
items.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerousIt is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it.The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. The match went off without trouble too and the Hednesford gang – known at home as the “schooligans” – were escorted safely back to the station by Cheshire police. It was just another weekend in English non-league football, where a wave of antisocial behaviour is causing concern and leading the UK Football Policing Unit (UKFPU) to declare it its “most important” priority. As the disorder continues, a question remains: how long will it be before teenage trouble-making becomes something more dangerous? Continue reading...

items.title: Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami confirm two absences for the regular season finale vs Charlotte
items.description:
Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami close the regular season against Charlotte with a growing injury list and a playoff position still at stake. 
Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami will close the 2026 MLS regular season without some of their young defenders. The Herons host Charlotte FC on Saturday at Nu Stadium in the last match before the playoffs, and the injury list has grown.



According to Inter Miami insider Jose Armando, Fricio Caicedo and Cesar Abadia are confirmed absences for the match. Caicedo, an 18-year-old Ecuadorian defender who joined on loan, is dealing with a knee problem, while Abadia’s absence has not been detailed.



The pair join two other players who will not be available either. Tadeo Allende and Mateo Silvetti have been ruled out for the rest of the season. The former Celta Vigo forward underwent arthroscopic surgery on his right knee in Barcelona and is listed with a season-ending injury on the club’s website.



On the other hand, the former Newell’s Old Boys forward, who recorded three goals and four assists in 14 MLS games before getting hurt, underwent surgery on his left shoulder after dislocating it, and the club said he will now focus on his recovery ahead of next season.




Back home. One last regular season showdown. 🏠⚽🔗 https://t.co/TaiIUx6Nzi pic.twitter.com/zkKNeexxto— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) November 4, 2026




Despite the absences, coach Kily Gonzalez otherwise has a relatively healthy squad. The team already secured its place in the postseason, with second place in the Eastern Conference still at stake, while Messi, who arrives with 26 goals, four ahead of Petar Musa, will try to clinch his second straight Golden Boot.



Inter Miami’s possible playoff rivals


        


Inter Miami will finish the regular season either second or third in the Eastern Conference. The Herons hold second place with 59 points, one more than New England Revolution, which visits Orlando City at the same time Miami hosts Charlotte. A win against Charlotte guarantees second place, while a draw would be enough unless New England wins.



If Miami ends up second, it will face the seventh seed in Round One. Today that spot belongs to FC Cincinnati, which has 46 points and hosts Nashville SC, but Philadelphia Union (47), Columbus Crew (44) and Orlando City (43) are all in the race for the last direct spot, so the rival could change.



If Miami finishes third, it will meet the sixth seed, currently Philadelphia Union with 47 points and a home match against Toronto FC. Cincinnati and Columbus could also climb to that position, which means Miami’s opponent will not be known until all matches end at the same time on Saturday.

items.title: Lionel Messi chases two unprecedented MLS records on the final day of the regular season
items.description:
Lionel Messi enters the final day of the MLS regular season with two chances to rewrite history: a record-breaking scoring title and a third MVP award. 
Lionel Messi has made a habit of breaking barriers in Major League Soccer, but the final day of the 2026 regular season could add two more entries to his collection. At 39 years old, the Inter Miami captain heads into the last matchday with a chance to achieve two feats that no player has accomplished in the league’s 31 years of history.



The first one is the Golden Boot. Messi arrives at the final match with 26 goals, four more than his closest pursuer, Dallas forward Petar Musa, and with the chance to become the first player in MLS history to win two consecutive scoring titles.



Several players have won the award more than once, among them Preki, Taylor Twellman, Jeff Cunningham, Chris Wondolowski and Bradley Wright-Phillips, but none has done it in back-to-back seasons.



The Argentine has been at the center of Inter Miami’s season once again. In 30 league matches, he has scored 26 goals and provided 14 assists, numbers that make him the main candidate for the individual awards this year.




Simplemente Leo Messi. 🔟 ✨ pic.twitter.com/sqiH0DzCef— Inter Miami CF (@InterMiamiCF) November 2, 2026




Inter Miami closes the regular season on Saturday against Charlotte FC, and Messi will have one last chance to extend his advantage over Musa. If the Dallas striker does not close the gap, the Golden Boot will go back to the Argentine, and with it a record that has eluded some of the best scorers in the league’s history.



A third MVP in three seasons


        


The second record is the MVP award. Messi is the main candidate to win his third Most Valuable Player award in three full seasons with Inter Miami, something that no player has achieved in MLS history. He already holds two, and with a third he would stand alone in the history of the league’s most prestigious individual honor.



Beyond his numbers, the Inter Miami star has kept the team among the top contenders in the East, a combination of impact and consistency that has defined each of his MVP-caliber campaigns since he arrived in 2023.



The regular season ends this weekend, but the story will continue through the playoffs, which begin on Nov. 18. For Messi, the chance to leave his mark twice in the same year, with a second Golden Boot and a third MVP, would only strengthen a legacy in American soccer that no one has been able to match.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo reportedly drops Al-Nassr exit bombshell after Portugal retirement as potential final appearance date emerges
items.description:
The Portuguese superstar is reportedly considering bringing his time in Saudi Arabia to an end, although the club hierarchy is determined to keep him in Riyadh. 
Cristiano Ronaldo could be approaching another major turning point in his career, with reports suggesting that his future at Al-Nassr is becoming increasingly uncertain following his retirement from international soccer. The Portuguese superstar is reportedly considering bringing his time in Saudi Arabia to an end, although the club hierarchy is determined to keep him in Riyadh.



At 41, Ronaldo remains one of Al-Nassr‘s most important players, both on and off the pitch. However, speculation surrounding his next move has intensified, with reports indicating that the 2026-27 campaign could represent the final chapter of his spell at the Saudi giant.



The latest speculation comes shortly after the 41-year-old announced his retirement from Portugal on November 5, 2026. He ended his international career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, leaving behind a record that made him the highest-scoring player in men’s international soccer. His decision means he can now concentrate entirely on club soccer without the demands of international breaks.



Under coach Ange Postecoglou, Al-Nassr will hope to benefit from his continued availability as the club pursues domestic and continental honors. Ronaldo is also approaching another extraordinary individual milestone. Following a hat-trick in Al-Nassr’s 5-3 victory over Al Kholood on October 29, he reached 985 official career goals, leaving him 15 short of the 1,000-goal target.



Ronaldo's hat-trick to take him to goal 985 🤩 pic.twitter.com/oxgu7aqua2— Roshn Saudi League (@SPL_EN) October 29, 2026 



The possibility of retirement has already been discussed by the forward himself. In an August 2026 interview with Vogue, he described the ongoing campaign as “probably my last year of football”, while expressing his desire to leave behind a remarkable legacy.



Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr future takes dramatic turn



According to 365Scores, Ronaldo has informed Al-Nassr officials that the ongoing season could be his last with the club. The report claims that the hierarchy is keen to extend his contract beyond its current expiration date in June 2027.



Al-Nassr is reportedly exploring ways to persuade the forward to remain for another season, while also considering how to honor his contribution if he decides to leave. A potential farewell match and a major celebration are among the plans being discussed, although neither Ronaldo’s departure nor any formal tribute has been confirmed.



Since arriving in Riyadh in early 2023, the Portuguese ace has helped transform the Knight of Najd’s international profile and attracted considerable attention to Saudi soccer. He also played a major role in the club’s reported 2025-26 Saudi Pro League title triumph, scoring 28 league goals during the campaign.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr celebrates with the Saudi Pro League Trophy.



When could Ronaldo make his final professional appearance?



While Ronaldo has yet to confirm whether he intends to retire after the current campaign, speculation has also emerged about when his final professional appearance could take place.



According to the official Saudi Pro League schedule, May 28, 2027, could become the date of Ronaldo’s final match if he decides to retire at the end of the season. The suggested occasion is particularly significant, as Ange Postecoglou’s players are scheduled to face fierce Riyadh rival Al-Hilal in the final round of the Saudi Pro League.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr is challenged by Nasser Al-Dawsari of Al Hilal.



The potential farewell would take place at Kingdom Arena, Al-Hilal’s home ground, giving Ronaldo the opportunity to end his career in one of Saudi Arabia’s biggest soccer rivalries. However, this remains an early speculative prediction rather than a confirmed retirement plan or official announcement.



For now, Al-Nassr is still hoping to convince their captain to extend his stay, and Ronaldo has several months remaining on his current contract. Whether he signs a new deal, pursues another challenge, or retires after reaching 1,000 goals remains uncertain, but his next decision could determine how one of soccer’s most remarkable careers comes to a close.

items.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
items.description: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing bodyThe total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times.That would mean direct income from the matchgoing fans came in five times as high in the United States, Canada and Mexico as it did at the last World Cup, in Qatar in 2022, when the total stood at $929m. While 2026’s expanded World Cup added 40 games to the schedule, the takings nevertheless went from an average of about $14.5m per match to about $48m. Continue reading...

items.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
items.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and UnitedAfter seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top.The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

items.description: Club’s predicament raises interesting questions about principles, both for individuals and the Premier LeagueI felt unbelievably ponderous. My head was made of Aztec stone. He kicked away from me. I got up and walked off. I was exceedingly hungry.Not my words. Also not the words of the Manchester City centre-back Marc Guéhi, despite what you were thinking there. items.description: Swindon manager has a history of viral outbursts but fans want a united club and manager they can supportIn Ian Holloway’s often madcap managerial orbit, this was simply the latest in a steady succession of eccentric outbursts. Eyes bulging as he spoke, he boomed the letter “D” and promptly stabbed himself in the chest with an imaginary dagger. Next came the letter “M” alongside a blow from another invisible knife. Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.”To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well).The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players.The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. items.title: The 10,000 treasures of the Marquis’ tomb
items.description: A staggering haul of more than 10,000 treasures have been unearthed from an ancient royal tomb in Jiangxi province. Some of the amazing artefacts discovered during the five-year excavation are now on show at the Capital Museum in Beijing. The tomb, near modern day Nanchang, is the last resting place of Liu He, who was emperor for just 27 days before being overthrown for his “lack of talent and morals”. items.title: IN PHOTOS: Tsunami barrier in Japan's northeastern coast
items.description: Four years after much of Japan's northeastern coast was devastated by a tsunami, a chain of cement sea walls stretching nearly 400km is under construction. Some of the walls will be five storeys high in places. items.title: A perfect stunt: Two Russian daredevils climb world’s second tallest building
items.description:
A video filmed using head mounted cameras of two gutsy Russians scaling China's Shanghai Tower without ropes or any climbing gear has gone viral.
Vadim Makhorov and Vitaliy Raskalov not only climbed to the top of the Shanghai Tower, but also scaled a crane on top of the building. The pair sneaked into the building site at midnight on Chinese New Year and spent almost two hours climbing up 120 floors to reach a height of 650 metres.
All photos by Imagine China.
